land.text: French Mauritania, independent from France on 28 November 1960; Cliopatria carries the land in its French Fifth Republic row for 1958-1960

predecessors.note: The political predecessor is the French West Africa federation (french-africa dossier); Cliopatria's French Africa row ends in 1957 and its French Fifth Republic row holds the land to 1960.

capitals.name: Nouakchott
capitals.note: 'When Senegal gained its independence that year, France chose Nouakchott as the site of the new capital of Mauritania.' The page does not give the year the town was founded or first used.

correction.text: Mauritania in its independence year: the Cliopatria 1961 shape unchanged, from 28 November 1960

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Mauritania shape begins in 1961; its infobox gives 'Independence from France: 28 November 1960'. In 1960 Cliopatria still draws the land inside French Fifth Republic (all 4,151 cells).
1.044 M km2 against the infobox's 1,030,000 km2 (ratio 1.01). The page records no boundary change between independence and 1976.

union.text: Tiris al-Gharbiya, 'roughly corresponding to the southern half of Rio de Oro': the southern third of Western Sahara

correction.text: for 1976 to 11 August 1979 the shape plus Tiris al-Gharbiyya, the southern third of Western Sahara that 'Mauritania took control of'; from August 1979 (1980 in yearly steps) the shape as drawn, because Mauritania 'withdrew all its forces' and Morocco annexed the area

keyframe_review.note: 1.053 M km2 for 1976-2023 against the infobox's 1,030,000 km2 (ratio 1.02). The shape is 38 cells (about 9,000 km2) larger than 1961, scattered along the northern frontier, and holds only 13 cells of the Western Sahara country polygon: it does not draw the southern third of Western Sahara in 1976-1979 and is the post-1979 outline for all its years. The ledger adds and removes Tiris al-Gharbiyya.
Same outline as 1976 at 1.053 M km2; no boundary change after 1979 on the pages opened.

region.text: Mauritania within its present frontier, without Tiris al-Gharbiyya

ledger.note: 28 November 1960: Mauritania becomes independent from France. Infobox: 'Independence from France: 28 November 1960'; 'In 1960, Mauritania became an independent nation.'

region.text: Tiris al-Gharbiya, 'roughly corresponding to the southern half of Rio de Oro': the southern third of Western Sahara

ledger.note: December 1975: Mauritanian troops take Tichla and La Guera. 'On 20 December, Mauritanian troops succeeded taking over Tichla and La Guera after two weeks of siege'; Spain had 'ceded the administrative control of the territory to Mauritania and Morocco on 14 November 1975'. The year is read from the page's 1975 sequence. The fighting is with the Polisario Front.

region.text: Tiris al-Gharbiya, 'roughly corresponding to the southern half of Rio de Oro': the southern third of Western Sahara

ledger.note: 1976: Mauritania annexes the southern part of Western Sahara. 'In 1976, Mauritania, along with Morocco, annexed the territory of Western Sahara'; the Western Sahara War page adds 'Mauritania took control of the southern third' and Morocco 'the northern two-thirds'. Spain had held the territory (Cliopatria's Francoist Spain shape holds all of it to 1975).

region.text: Tiris al-Gharbiya, 'roughly corresponding to the southern half of Rio de Oro': the southern third of Western Sahara

ledger.note: August 1979: Mauritania gives up Tiris al-Gharbiyya. 'A comprehensive peace treaty was signed on 5 August 1979' with the Polisario; the new Mauritanian government 'relinquished its own claims' and 'withdrew all its forces'; the area was 'unilaterally annexed by Morocco on 11 August 1979'. The Mauritania page says 'Mauritania withdrew in 1979'.

region.text: Tiris al-Gharbiya, 'roughly corresponding to the southern half of Rio de Oro': the southern third of Western Sahara

ledger.note: 5 August 1979: the peace treaty ends Mauritania's war with the Polisario. The new government, which took power in the summer-1978 coup, 'immediately agreed to a ceasefire with the Polisario' (no month on the page); the 5 August 1979 treaty is the end of the claim.

wars.name: Western Sahara War

zones.text: Tiris al-Gharbiya, 'roughly corresponding to the southern half of Rio de Oro': the southern third of Western Sahara

wars.outcome: Mauritania made peace with the Polisario on 5 August 1979 and withdrew; Morocco annexed Tiris al-Gharbiyya on 11 August 1979. The monitored ceasefire between Morocco and the Polisario came into effect on 6 September 1991.
wars.note: Mauritania's part runs 1975-1979. The page says the Polisario launched a raid on Nouakchott in which its leader El Ouali was killed and struck the Zouerate iron mines repeatedly (no dates on the page); the Daddah regime 'fell in summer 1978 to a coup d'etat' (the Mauritania page gives 10 July 1978). The Mauritania page says the Polisario was 'heavily armed and supported by Algeria'.

wars.name: Mauritania-Senegal border conflict
wars.outcome: The page opened gives only the opening incidents; no territorial change.
wars.note: 'This ethnic discord was evident during intercommunal violence that broke out in April 1989'; 'On 9 April 1989, Mauritanian guards killed two Senegalese.' Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered; a gap-filler should open the war's own article.

certainty.note: The frontiers run through the Sahara and the Senegal valley and the pages opened give no boundary treaty or survey for any of them; the Western Sahara frontier was moved in 1976 and 1979 and is soft throughout. Judgment, not a source.

sources.title: Mauritania
sources.note: Independence 28 November 1960, area 1,030,000 km2, Nouakchott, 1976 annexation and 1979 withdrawal, the 1989 incidents.

sources.title: Western Sahara War
sources.note: Madrid Accords 14 November 1975, Tichla and La Guera 20 December, the southern third, the 5 August 1979 treaty, Morocco's annexation on 11 August 1979, the 1991 ceasefire.

notes: Budget: 2 pages, met. Cliopatria's 1976-2023 shape does not include the southern third of Western Sahara for 1976-1979; the ledger adds it (gain 1976 from francoist-spain, loss 1979 to morocco) and the keyframe verdict says so. The 1961 and 1976 shapes differ by 38 cells scattered along the northern frontier (a refit of the outline, not an annexation); the pages give no boundary change to explain it. The Madrid Accords (14 November 1975) are administrative control, not sovereignty, per the War page; the partition agreement and its date are not on the pages opened (April 1976 is not asserted). The Mauritania page is silent on the Madrid Accords and on the year Nouakchott was founded. Counterparts: francoist-spain (ends 1975; its Cliopatria shape holds all of Western Sahara), morocco (Cliopatria's Morocco shape excludes Western Sahara, so its dossier should carry the gain of Tiris al-Gharbiyya in 1979 and of the north in 1976), 'Polisario Front' (a name; the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic may get a dossier from af-08-x as 'Western Sahara'). Gazetteer name needed: 'Tiris al-Gharbiyya' (the Moroccan Oued ed-Dahab region plus the Polisario-held strip east of the berm roughly covers it). Gabon and Ivory Coast, not Mauritania, recognised Biafra (Civil War page).
